_file_comment: Chronicles of Darkness — Mortals+ data file.
This file has three sections: CONFIGURATION, then CONTENT.
CONFIGURATION keys drive the app structure and should be edited carefully.
CONTENT keys are lists of game entries freely added, removed, or replaced.
Use the in-app Data Library import/export to share or update content safely.
_skills_comment: skill_definitions: ordered list of all skills available on the sheet.
key:      internal identifier used in saved characters (do not change after use)
label:    display name shown on the sheet (can be changed freely)
The 'athletics' key is referenced in the Defense formula.
Renaming its label is safe; changing its key will break Defense calculation.
To add a skill: append an entry. To remove: delete the entry.
Skills are shown in the order listed here.

skill_definitions.label: Athletics
skill_definitions._note: athletics key is used in the Defense formula — renaming the label is safe, but do not change the key

_sections_comment: section_definitions: ordered registry of every toggleable sheet section.
Each entry: { key, label, group, zone, order, type, default, [state_key], [max_rating], [max], [beats_key], [xp_key] }
key:        unique identifier for this section (used in sectionConfig)
label:      display name shown in the Sheet Configuration panel and on the PDF
group:      config panel group header: Mortal | Hunter | (future splats)
zone:       where on the sheet this section appears:
header            — character header row
beats             — beats/XP tracker row (between header and full-width-top)
full-width-top    — full-width area below beats, above the two columns
left-column       — left column (skills area)
right-column      — right column (traits/conditions area)
full-width-bottom — full-width area below the two columns
order:      sort order within the zone (lower = higher on sheet)
type:       rendering type — see list below
default:    true = visible by default, false = hidden by default
state_key:  STATE field this section reads/writes (defaults to key if omitted)
max_rating: for rated-list — maximum dot rating (default 5)
max:        for dot-track — number of dots (default 10)
beats_key:  for beats-xp — STATE key for the beats counter (default: 'beats')
xp_key:     for beats-xp — STATE key for the experience counter (default: 'experience')
top_label:   for quinpar-wheel — label for the top value (default: 'Quintessence')
bottom_label: for quinpar-wheel — label for the bottom value (default: 'Paradox')
Section types:
attributes      — the 9 core attributes (special renderer)
skills          — the 27 skills with rote/specialty (special renderer)
derived-traits  — health, willpower, defense, initiative, speed (special renderer)
dot-track       — a simple 1–N dot track (e.g. Integrity, Humanity)
header-fields   — text fields in the character header
beats-xp        — a beats counter + XP counter pair (zone: beats)
line-list       — a simple list of text lines (e.g. Aspirations, Touchstones)
named-list      — collapsible cards with name + description (e.g. Tilts, Tactics)
rated-list      — collapsible cards with name + rating + description (e.g. Merits, Endowments)
resource-track  — 20 manually-toggled squares in 2 rows of 10 (Mana, Essence, Vitae)
arcana-block    — fixed rated list from the section's fields array (Mage Arcana)
renown-block    — five named 5-dot tracks in a single block (Werewolf Renown)
forms-block     — live reference table showing per-form calculated stats
weapons         — weapon cards with full weapon fields (special renderer)
armor           — armor cards with full armor fields (special renderer)
equipment       — equipment cards with full equipment fields (special renderer)
textarea        — a multi-line text area (e.g. Notes, The Code)
dot-square-track — dot row (max rating) above square row (current value), like Willpower but data-driven (e.g. Clarity)
_presets_comment: Applying a preset does a full reset — all sections are set to the values listed.
Every section key must be present in each preset.
To add a preset: add an entry with a name and a config covering all section keys.
The 'Mortal' preset represents the default starting configuration.

merits.name: Area of Expertise
merits.desc: Requires 2 Resolve and 1 Skill Specialty. Choose a Specialty to assign to this Merit. Forgo the +1 bonus afforded by a Specialty, in exchange for a +2.

merits.name: Ambidextrous
merits.desc: Available only at character creation. Your character does not suffer the -2 penalty for using his off hand in combat or to perform other actions.

anthem_charms.name: Anthem
anthem_charms.desc:
***BASIC ACTION***
**Action**: Instant
**Dice Pool**: Presence + Expression + Inner Light--target's Composure (if resisted).
**Duration**: Special. Anthem lasts for at least two turns, plus one additional turn for each charge spent on its duration. The caster can spend an instant action at any point later in the scene to continue their performance and 'refresh' Anthem, starting it up again without spending additional resources or rolling again.
**Scaling**: The number of successes determines the difficulty to resist the Anthem and its ability to counteract other sonic, performance, or emotional effects.
**Exceptional Success**: Increase the number of *charges* by 2.
**Basic Action**: The Princess delivers a *performance* to an *audience*, which evokes a *feeling* and applies the Stirring Performance Tilt
-A *performance* is 'an act of self-expression through some manner of live artistic communication.'
-The *audience* is 'everyone who can directly experience the *performance* out to a distance of roughly 20 yards.'
-The *feeling* is 'an emotion of your choice, evoked in the *audience*, that can encourage certain actions and discourage others.'
When you cast Anthem, you gain a number of *charges* equal to your Inner Light. Each *charge* you spend on the basic action increases the duration before you need to resume your *performance* by 1 turn. These *charges* can also be expended to enhance many Upgrades. While Anthem is active, your performance continues without you taking actions, maybe without you even visibly creating it: it can become the 'background music' or the atmospheric groove that just plays in the environment.
The Stirring Performance Tilt (**p. 271**) is keyed to the *feeling* the Anthem applied. While Anthem is active, Stirring Performance grants +2 to all dice pools that are taken in line with the Anthem’s *feeling*.
Nobody can benefit from the Stirring Performance of more than one character at a time (but multiple Princesses can cast it as a teamwork action to boost the main performer). The caster is *not* part of their own *audience* unless another ability says they are. Anthem conflicts with other Anthems as well as similar musical or sonic effects like a Sin-Eater's Dirge or mass emotional manipulation abilities, at the discretion of the Storyteller. When Anthem causes a Clash of Wills, add the successes from the Anthem spell or the other effect to the dice pool for the Clash of Wills as if it was a cooperation roll. Rocking harder will always make your spell more powerful.
**Invocation**: The act of performing and communicating through your performance is considered the Invocation for this Charm; you don't need to shout something special in addition to that.
**Regalia**: Anthem Regalia is all instruments of performance. Usually, this is a musical instrument of some kind--a flute, a lyre, an ocarina, a steel drum, a BC Rich Warlock electric guitar, a magical cordless microphone, a chakram tambourine, a piano synthesizer or set of DJ turntables that hover in front of their user. For other forms of performance, Regalia is something used to do the performance, or something that augments it: tap dancing shoes could be Regalia, but so could the decorated dreadlocks that whirl and whip with the movement of a capoeira dancer. Spotlights might hover in the air to cast their light on the performer when she's ready for her solo.

anthem_charms.name: Bassline Anthem
anthem_charms.desc:
Gifted to Princesses of Flowers--allows Composure to be used instead of Presence

*'I'm gonna fight 'em off. A seven nation army couldn't hold me back.'*

You may expend *charges* to enhance the dice bonus conferred by your Stirring Performance Tilt. One *charge* enhances it to a +3 bonus, three *charges* enhance it to a +4 bonus, and six *charges* enhance it to a +5 bonus.

anthem_charms.name: Breakup Anthem
anthem_charms.desc:
*'I don't wanna be a fool for you/in this game for two/so I'm leaving you behind!'*

Your Anthem can reflexively trigger a Clash of Wills against someone using a supernatural ability on or in your *audience,* even if it doesn't directly oppose the Anthem. If you win the Clash, the opposing spell or ability fizzles out, unable to throw off the groove. This only works once per scene, plus one additional time for each *charge* spent, and you must spend a Wisp each time it triggers.

anthem_charms.name: Face-Melting Anthem
anthem_charms.desc:
Gifted to Princesses of Storms--allows Dexterity to be used instead of Presence

*'Do ya wanna, do ya wanna dance--with a JAWBREAKER!?'*

Each time anyone in the *audience* acts against the *feeling* you inspire, they make a Resolve + Composure roll contested against this Charm. On a failure, they immediately take 2 Bashing damage, plus one more for each *charge* spent.

anthem_charms.name: Glamorous Anthem
anthem_charms.desc:
Gifted to Princesses of Mirrors--allows Manipulation to be used instead of Presence

*'Watch out for my medallion, my diamonds are reckless/It feels like a midget is hangin' from my necklace!'*

The overwhelming charisma and sparkle of your *performance* is hard to deny: anyone in the *audience* with Composure less than your activation successes has a -2 dice penalty to all actions that run counter to your *feeling*, plus an additional -1 for each *charge* spent.

anthem_charms.name: Harmonized Anthem
anthem_charms.desc:
*'If you're ever in trouble, I'll be there on the double, just send for me oh baby!'*

Your Anthem applies two different Stirring Performance Tilts simultaneously. They must be distinct *feelings*, but any bonuses and penalties from them stack so long as an action fulfills / runs counter to both of them.
When you do this, the same Upgrades apply to each Stirring Performance, but you divvy up the *charges* separately.

anthem_charms.name: Heart-Rending Anthem
anthem_charms.desc:
Gifted to Princesses of Tears--allows Wits to be used instead of Presence

*'Feels like pins and needles in my heart, so long I can feel it tearing me apart...'*

Anyone in the *audience* acting against the *feeling* you inspire requires a Resolve + Composure roll contested against this Charm. On a failure, the action costs a Willpower. This can only drain one Willpower per scene, plus an additional Willpower for each *charge* spent.

anthem_charms.name: Inspirational Anthem
anthem_charms.desc:
Gifted to Princesses of Jewels--allows Composure to be used instead of Presence

*'We are the champions, my friend... And we'll keep on fighting 'til the end...'*

Your Stirring Performance Tilt now also applies a variant of the Inspired Condition: once per scene, when taking an action in line with your *feeling*, the *audience* may reduce the number of Successes required for an Exceptional Success by one, plus one more for each *charge* spent. If they get that Exceptional Success, they regain 1 Willpower.
Using this Upgrade costs 1 Willpower. A given character can only gain this Willpower once per chapter per performer; if you have multiple Princesses who perform for each other to restore communal Willpower that's not 'an exploit' that's 'forming a band.'

anthem_charms.name: Instructional Anthem
anthem_charms.desc:
Gifted to Princesses of Currents--allows Intelligence to be used instead of Presence

*'You've gotta do the cooking by the book. You know you can't be lazy!'*

Choose up to 2 *audience* members, plus one more for each *charge* spent. Pick a Skill that one of them has, or that you have. While affected by Stirring Performance, every chosen *audience* member has that Skill exactly as the original character has it, including Skill dots, specialties, and relevant Merits.

anthem_charms.name: Jumpin' Jack Anthem
anthem_charms.desc:
*'I was booorn in a crossfire hurricane! And I hooowled at my Ma in the drivin' rain! But it's all right now, in fact it's a gas!'*

Channel the power of your *audience's* blazing spirit, lead a performance that crackles with the brilliant power of the Light of Hope. Any time an *audience* member willingly spends a Willpower, or scores an Exceptional Success on a roll to support the performance (dance, sing along, calland-response, chime in, provide setups to punchlines, clap and stamp their feet, etc.), you gain a Wisp and may give that Wisp to any other *audience* member that can use it.

anthem_charms.name: Liberating Anthem
anthem_charms.desc:
Gifted to Princesses of Spades--allows Dexterity to be used instead of Presence

*'Back off your riles, back off your jive! 'Cause I'm sick of not living to stay alive!'*

Any *audience* member currently under a mental or psychological Tilt may make an appropriate roll to throw it off. For each *charge* spent, they may try this roll again on a subsequent turn.

anthem_charms.name: Lingering Anthem
anthem_charms.desc:
*'Thanks, you've been a lovely audience, we're out!'*

The basic effect of Stirring Performance--+2 to die rolls in line with the *feeling*--persists for the rest of the scene. None of the other effects that you spent *charges* on persist.

anthem_charms.name: Recorded Anthem
anthem_charms.desc:
*'Put another dime in the jukebox, baby.'*

Your *performance* can be captured in some form that the *audience* can access later. The *performance* will only apply the effect of Anthem once; after that, the *performance* may be stirring but it won't apply a Tilt.
This means you can make a musical or oratory *performance* through a record of your sound and voice. It also means you can make your *performance* in the form of any other art that can convey your emotions and doesn't require you to be there to perform it: a sculpture, a written poem, even a loaf of bread baked with absolute care and passion.

anthem_charms.name: Romantic Anthem
anthem_charms.desc:
Gifted to Princesses of Swords--allows Intelligence to be used instead of Presence

*'I can't see me lovin' nobody but you, for all my life...'*

Everyone under your Stirring Performance Tilt is considered to have an Impression for Social Maneuvering one stage better than it would otherwise be, and a similar positive predisposition for non-Maneuvering purposes.

anthem_charms.name: Secret Anthem
anthem_charms.desc:
*'This one goes out to a very special someone in the audience right now.'*

Your *audience* includes only those people you choose, not everyone who can perceive the *performance*.

anthem_charms.name: Thrilling Anthem
anthem_charms.desc:
*'Girl, I can thrill you more than any ghoul can ever dare try!'*

You can lead your *audience* in specific actions--anyone under the effect of your Stirring Performance who doesn't resist can use their turn to mimic your actions exactly. The *audience* will use your Skills and Attributes to make rolls this way, but they can't do supernatural things they don't otherwise have the ability for. 
If you apply this Upgrade, it costs **two** *charges* for each turn to extend your Stirring Performance.

anthem_charms.name: Window-Rattling Anthem
anthem_charms.desc:
*'Are you ready to rock? Because I'm gonna blow your hair to the BACK OF THIS AUDITORIUM!'*

Your Anthem affects a large enough area to make an *audience* of everyone in a stadium's worth of space, all the way up to the cheap seats.

anthem_charms.name: Max Volume Anthem
anthem_charms.desc:
*'These go to eleven.'*

This is an advanced Upgrade. It counts as two Upgrades when applied to a Charm.

Your Anthem overflows with power. You gain double the *charges* for enhancing your Anthem Upgrades, and each Upgrade gets the effect of one *charge* for free.

anthem_charms.name: Tribute Anthem
anthem_charms.desc:
*'This is not the greatest song in the world, no. This is just a tribute.'*

This is an advanced Upgrade. It counts as two Upgrades when applied to a Charm.

You can mimic and repeat an Instant action performed by an *audience* member under your Stirring Performance Tilt, so long as it's something you understand how to do; you *do not have to have a power or Merit you'd otherwise need.* Use the casting roll for Anthem to resolve this action instead of the normal dice pool, but you can't get more successes than the action you mimic.

buster_charms.name: Buster
buster_charms.desc:
*'HERE I GO! This hand of mine is burning red! Its loud roar tells me to grasp victory! ERUPTING... BURNING... FINGER!'*

***BASIC ACTION***
**Action**: Instant
**Dice Pool**: Inner Light + Buster Overcharge
**Duration**: Instant
**Scaling**: Determines the damage of the attack.
**Exceptional Success**: More successes are their own reward.
**Basic Action**: You accumulate Buster Overcharge dice when you spend Wisps. When you cast Buster, you gather and discharge your fighting spirit and will into a devastating, vivid blast of energy at a single target.
This Charm is a ranged attack. Any penalties or bonuses that apply to ranged attacks, including but not limited to aiming, cover, and concealment, apply to this Charm's activation roll. Buster's attack range is Short (up to about 30 meters), and there are no penalties for firing at Close or melee range if you don't use a Regalia Weapon for it; Regalia Weapons that have penalties at this range will apply the penalty to the Buster as well. A Princess may choose to deal bashing or lethal damage with her Buster each time she casts it.
**Special**: A Princess's Buster accumulated power over time; just as her Willpower filters into her Wisps as her resolve purifies, the Wisps she expends on her own magic rise to the surface of her fighting spirit, ready to surge outward in the form of pure power. Every time a Princess spends a Wisp on anything other than casting Buster, she gets two Buster Overcharge dice. When she casts Buster, she can consume any number of her Buster Overcharge dice to add to the activation roll. If not spent, Buster Overcharge dice are lost at the end of a chapter
**Invocation**: Buster must always be shouted out and declared as loud as you god damn can. Time will appear to stop as you call out the name, do the moves, and display the light show
**Regalia**: Buster Regalia is impossible to ignore. It might be a magic wand or an unfolding vector cannon. It might be a regal scepter or a toy raygun. A whirling set of ribbons that bind together into an elegant spiral pattern or a spiked, sparking cybernetic arm cannon. Whatever it is, it's going to appear *vivid,* attention-grabbing, and anyone who looks at it will know it's Serious Business. The only thing they have in common is that they are something you can point at your enemy while you shout out everything your attack comes from and everyone it protects. All Buster Regalia are ranged weapons with the 'Buster' tag; the Buster inherits properties from the weapon except for Burst and Autofire.

buster_charms.name: BOTTOMLESS INFINITY BUSTER!
buster_charms.desc:
When you cast buster, don't roll for it or consume your Buster Overcharge dice yet. Your Buster fires off on your *next* turn, taking your movement and action. If you took damage from a melee attack in the intervening time, the Buster fails. Otherwise, resolved the dice pool then, using your target's current cover, concealment, range, etc, and allowing them to apply their Defense--but **double** your dice pool before subtracting any penalties.
This Upgrade can be applied multiple times, and each time you do, increase the number of turns you can charge it by 1, and each turn you charge it adds your base dice pool to the activation roll again.

buster_charms.name: ECHO BURST BUSTER!
buster_charms.desc: When you cast Buster, roll all your Buster Overcharge dice separately from the rest. (Penalties are subtracted from your normal dice first, not your Overcharge dice.) Any die that doesn’t result in a success isn’t consumed and can be rolled on your next Buster attack.

buster_charms.name: EVERLASTING DEVASTATION BUSTER!
buster_charms.desc: Your Buster damage repeats against anyone and anything it strikes. Each subsequent turn, the target must succeed on a reflexive (Resolve or Stamina) + Potency roll, penalized by the activation successes of the Buster hit, or take the Buster attack’s weapon damage again. This roll gets a stacking +2 bonus each round after the first.

buster_charms.name: GIGADRIVE EXCEED BUSTER!
buster_charms.desc:
Gifted to all Princesses, regardless of Queen

This is the basic Buster ability, and everyone starts with it for good reason: it’s pretty much always useful. Gigadrive Exceed can be applied to a Buster multiple times, and each time you do, it increases the Buster’s dice pool by +2. The bonus dice given by Gigadrive Exceed can’t exceed the normal number of Buster Overcharge dice you rolled.

buster_charms.name: PETADRIVE ANNIHILATION BUSTER!
buster_charms.desc:
Gigadrive Exceed's angry older sister who's been sent to juvie multiple times. Petadrive Annihilation Buster grants +4 dice to your Buster, it can be applied multiple times, AND it isn’t restricted by how many Buster Overcharge dice you have.
It has two drawbacks: One, you cannot use free Upgrades to apply Petadrive Annihilation—every application costs a Wisp. Second, you must spend every single Buster Overcharge die you have on it, which must be at least four.

buster_charms.name: PINPOINT SNIPER BUSTER!
buster_charms.desc: The range of your Buster extends to Long (up to roughly 300 meters). You also hit with pinpoint accuracy, reducing penalties for distance, called shots, and tiny targets by your Inner Light.

buster_charms.name: RELENTLESS HOMING BUSTER!
buster_charms.desc: Your Buster can go around corners and over obstacles. You still have to know where your target is to within 2 meters—a spotter is very helpful—and they can still attempt to get out of the way of the attack when it’s coming, but you ignore line-of-sight, cover, and the target’s Defense if they have an effect that lets them apply it to ranged attacks.

buster_charms.name: UPHEAVAL SLAM BUSTER!
buster_charms.desc: Choose an environmental Tilt (subject to Storyteller approval) when you gain this Upgrade. Anyone hit by your Buster is subject to that Tilt until they somehow escape from it. Most often used for Tilts that affect movement and visibility (like a blizzard or uneven terrain due to lush overgrowth).

buster_charms.name: WITHERING DEMONBANE BUSTER!
buster_charms.desc: You empower your Buster with occult magic and apply the supernatural Bane or Ban properties of one other kind of event or material to it, causing the Buster to serve as that Bane or Ban. Pick one kind of Bane when you buy this Upgrade that you may always apply (standards like sunlight, fire, silver, salt, jade, tungsten, etc). When you come into contact with the source of another type of Bane or Ban, you can apply it to your Buster once in the next 24 hours (if you have the source on you, of course, you can just apply it again immediately and reflexively).

buster_charms.name: CLEANSING DAYLIGHT BUSTER!
buster_charms.desc:
This is an advanced Upgrade. It counts as two Upgrades when applied to a Charm.

The blistering, radiant energy of your Buster sears away magical effects in its path. When targeted at someone who has active magical effects that can be subject to a Clash of Wills, this Buster forces a Clash against one of them (either one of your choice, or one at random if you don’t know.)
Your successes on the Clash of Wills can’t exceed the successes you rolled for Buster. If you succeed, the magical effect is suppressed for the scene.

buster_charms.name: HYPER-EXPLOSIVE BUSTER!
buster_charms.desc:
This is an advanced Upgrade. It counts as two Upgrades when applied to a Charm.

Your Buster is now an explosive (**CofD: Hurt Locker, p.134**). The damage bonus of your Buster Regalia is the base damage of the explosion, and resolve your Buster roll as the Force of the explosion. There is no ground zero to this explosion, but the primary blast area is equal to four times your Inner Light in meters.
If you apply this Upgrade, you only roll half of the Buster Overcharge dice you spend, rounded up. The other half are lost, diffused out over the blast area.

buster_charms.name: JUDGEMENT LIGHT BUSTER!
buster_charms.desc:
This is an advanced Upgrade. It counts as two Upgrades when applied to a Charm.

When your Buster targets any being with a Potency Trait, roll additional dice equal to that Trait. This can’t provide more dice than the total number of Buster Overcharge dice you spent. (The same Overcharge can be “counted” for Judgment Light and Gigadrive Exceed, so between the two Upgrades they can add two dice for each Overcharge you spend.)

conjure_charms.name: Conjure
conjure_charms.desc:
***BASIC ACTION***
**Action**: Extended. Each roll is one turn. No matter how many rolls you make for a single casting of Conjure, it only takes one Wisp.
**Dice Pool**: Manipulation + Science + Inner Light.
**Duration**: One scene.
**Scaling**: Successes determine the Size of the thing you can *summon*.
**Exceptional Success**: You complete the summoning so quickly that the action was reflexive and you can still act this turn.
**Basic Action**: At some time before using Conjure, you must *attune* to an *object* or an *actor* at no cost (you can *attune* to any number of things, but it gets hard to keep track of more than 3 times your current Inner Light worth of things). When you cast Conjure, you start to *summon* that *object* or *actor* from its point of origin. You must accumulate a number of successes on the extended casting roll to equal the *object* or *actor*'s Size. If you summon something of Size 0, you treat it as summoning something of Size 1.
-You *attune* to something by 'being familiar with and having spent a significant amount of time in its presence and specially marking it in some way.'
-To *summon* is to 'magically transport an *object* or *actor* from wherever it currently is to a spot directly in front of you.'
-An *object* is 'a piece of equipment that falls in the 'physical object' category (**CofD, p 100**).' Without the Upgrade to do so, you can't *summon* 'mystical equipment;' the magic aura of being *summoned* messes with the mystical qualities in some way. You can't *summon* an object that someone else is using or otherwise attending to.
-An *actor* is 'your Shikigami.' If you take any combat actions, the stress will cause the link to shatter and the *actor* will return to its point of origin. You can't summon an *actor* who doesn't agree to be summoned, and can send a short message to any *actor* you attempt to summon explaining why they should accept.
The *object* or *actor* is ready to use on the turn after it is *summoned*. You can only have one *actor* summoned at a time, but any number of *objects*. The *object* or *actor* will return to its point of origin at the end of the scene unless it was destroyed or consumed. For example, if you *summon* some food and eat it, you won't have the energy sucked out of your body, but the bowl it came in would return to wherever it came from.
**Invocation**: Conjure must be Invoked by shouting or declaring a call to what you are summoning, what literal or metaphorical thing you take it from, or how you summon it.
**Regalia**: Conjure Regalia usually takes the form of something that the conjured thing will pass through (even without Conjure Portal), a representation of the thing you summon, or some manifestation of how a conjured thing is tied to you. A ring might expand to the diameter of a hula hoop for a box of supplies to fall through, or a magician's hat might produce a stream of rabbits. Little plastic miniatures or a quickly folded origami vehicle might grow into the form of the real thing. Something could be called over with puppet string, or a fishing pole and line.

armor.name: Reinforced Clothing
armor.notes: This armor is concealed. Covers torso, arms, and legs.

equipment.name: Flashlight
equipment.desc: Die bonus subtracts from any penalties due to darkness, and adds to any rolls to search in the dark. Some can also be used as a club. Also can blind a subject. Roll Dexterity + Athletics, subtracting opponent's Defense. The victim’s player. If your character scores more successes than the subject, the subject is blinded for one turn. Victims with especially acute senses are blinded for two turns.

equipment.name: Smartphone
equipment.desc: Increases dice bonus to +2 if bought at Availability 3. A smartphone with camera, GPS, and internet access. Battery lasts approximately one day of moderate use.

tilts.name: Arm Wrack
tilts.desc: One of the character's arms is damaged and unusable. They cannot use two-handed weapons or take actions requiring both arms. Any action suffers a -2 offhand penalty if taken with the offhand. Ended when the injury is healed.

tilts.name: Beaten Down
tilts.desc: The player must spend a point of Willpower each time he wants the character to take a violent action. Ends when the character surrenders.

conditions.name: Blind
conditions.desc: Any rolls requiring sight may only use a chance die. If another sense can be reasonably substituted, make the roll at -3 instead.

conditions.name: Inspired
conditions.desc: When your character takes an action pertaining to that inspiration, you may resolve this Condition. Gain a Willpower point, and consider the roll an Exceptional Success on three successes, instead of five

atavisms.name: Example Atavism
atavisms.desc: Add atavism entries here. Fields: name, desc.

nightmares.name: Example Nightmare
nightmares.desc: Add nightmare entries here. Fields: name, desc.

contracts.name: Cloak of Night (Common)
contracts.desc:
**Regalia:** Shield 
**Cost**: 1 Glamour
**Dice Pool**: None
**Action**: Instant
Effects: Must be invoked where vision roll penalties are applied. Affects a number of willing companions equal to dots in Dexterity. Stealth rolls gain a bonus of half the character's Wyrd rating and hide all affected characters as long as they don't draw attention to themselves.
**Darkling**: The Darkling and her companions retain the benefits of this Contract even if they attract attention to themselves.
**Ogre**: The Ogre may substitute Stamina for Dexterity for hiding companions.
**Loophole**: The changeling and her companions don black articles of clothing that mark them as sneaks and rogues.

contracts.name: Boon of the Scuttling Spider (Common)
contracts.desc:
**Cost**: 1 Glamour.
**Dice Pool**: None
**Action**: Instant.
**Effects**: Character can move along walls, ceilings, or slick surfaces at normal Speed.
**Beast**: May use the restrain in a grapple as though he had rolled an exceptional success.
**Darkling**: Gain a two-die bonus to stealth while scuttling across impossible surfaces.
**Loophole**: Changeling swallows a live spider.

pledges.name: Example Pledge
pledges.desc: Add pledge entries here. Fields: name, desc.

demonic_form.name: Armored Plates
demonic_form.desc:
**Modification**
**System**: Armor provides full coverage with a 3/2 rating and a -1 Defense and Speed penalty.

demonic_form.name: Environmental Resistance
demonic_form.desc:
**Technology**
**System**: The demon is immune to the adverse effects from all Environmental Tilts.

demonic_form.name: Wings
demonic_form.desc:
**Propulsion**
**System**: The demon is capable of flight and has a species factor of 10 to his Speed while flying.

embeds.name: Alibi
embeds.desc:
**Mundane**
**Dice Pool**: Manipulation + Stealth
**Action**: Instant
**Dramatic Failure**: The demon's Cover appears but not anywhere useful for an alibi. The demon has no idea where it appeared or what the consequences will be.
**Failure**: No effect. Cannot be used again for the target scene.
**Success**: The demon separates himself from his Cover for a scene. The cover is able to make small talk but not make dice rolls or take significant action. If the cover dies, the demon drops to Cover 0 unless he has another Cover to shift to or pact to call in. During this scene the demon can take any actions he wishes without fear his deeds will be traced back to his cover. As such, during that scene the demon cannot be compromised by taking actions antithetical to that Cover. Exploits and demonic form powers still compromise normally.
**Exceptional Success**: As above, but the cover possesses more self-awareness. If threatened, it leaves the area and vanishes when out of sight.

embeds.name: Common Misconception
embeds.desc:
**Vocal**
**Dice Pool**: Manipulation + Science
**Action**: Reflexive
**Dramatic Failure**: The information that the demon produces strengthens the target's argument. Add the demon's Primum to the target's Skill roll. The demon gains the Discredited Condition (-3 on all attempts to convince any witnesses to this exchange of anything for the rest of the scene). The demon can resolve this Condition by succeeding on a roll using the same Skill that the target was using, but achieving more successes than the target did.
**Failure**: No effect; the target's roll is unaffected.
**Success**: The "fact" that the demon produces undermines the target's ability. Apply a penalty equal to the Embed successes or the demon's Primum (whichever is higher) to the target's Skill roll.
**Exceptional Success**: The target fails the Skill roll outright and loses a point of Willpower.

embeds.name: Ambush
embeds.desc:
**Instrumental**
**Dice Pool**: Wits + Stealth
**Action**: Instant
**Dramatic Failure**: The demon prepares for the ambush, but has missed some critical detail. When the target arrives, the demon is surprised and any allies that were planning to benefit from this Embed must roll to see if they are surprised.
**Failure**: No effect. The demon and her allies must roll for initiative normally.
**Success**: The demon positions herself (and, if she wishes, allies up to her Primum rating) such that when their enemy enters the area, the enemy is automatically surprised. The enemy cannot act during the first turn of combat.
**Exceptional Success**: As above, except the demon can cover as many allies as she wishes with this Embed's effects.

exploits.name: Affliction
exploits.desc:
**Example Prerequisites**: Deafen, Recurring Hallucinations
**Dice Pool**: Strength + Medicine + Primum vs Stamina or Resolve + Supernatural Tolerance.
**Action**: Instant
**Cost**: 1 Aether
**Dramatic Failure**: The demon suffers the effects of the Affliction herself. Any Condition or Tilt thus gained remain until the demon assumes demonic form.
**Failure**: The target is not afflicted.
**Success**: The demon curses the target, and may impose one Condition or Tilt. Appropriate choices include Madness, Poisoned, Sick, Shunned, and Mute. The demon can also specify and outward sign of Affliction - a disfigurement, an alteration to the target's voice or smell, or any other effect that marks the character.
The Affliction remains until the demon removes it. It can generate Beats for the character, but its usual resolution does not apply. The Affliciton can be removed through magical or supernatural means, at the Storyteller's discretion.
**Exceptional Success**: The demon may add more Conditions or Tilts at a cost of one Aether and one Willpower point each.

exploits.name: Hellfire
exploits.desc:
**Example Prerequisites**: Check Backdrop, Merciless Gunman
**Dice Pool**: Presence + Firearms + Primum
**Action**: Reflexive
**Cost**: 1 Aether
**Dramatic Failure**: The gun explodes, inflicting aggravated damage to the demon (and the gun's wielder, if applicable) equal to the demon's Primum.
**Failure**: The Exploit does not work and the gun is unaffected.
**Success**: The gun inflicts aggravated damage for the remainder of the scene. It's other capabilities are unaffected.
**Exceptional Success**: As above, but the player adds the demon's Primum to the weapon's damage rating.

_hunter_content_comment: endowments: Hunter endowments from compacts and conspiracies.

endowments.name: Benediction
endowments.desc: Each point of Benediction grants access to an additional Virtuous Ritual and adds a die to the ritual dice pool.

endowments.name: Castigation: Sense Weakness
endowments.desc: Spend 1 Willpower and roll Wits + Empathy vs Finesse. On a success, gain the Informed Condition about the subject. On a failure, learn nothing. On a dramatic failure, gain the Spooked Condition.

endowments.name: Elixir
endowments.desc: Each dot of Elixir provides access to one additional recipe and adds a die to the Elixir dice pool.

tactics.name: Identification
tactics.desc:
**Requirements**: Primary actor: Occult 2
**Action**: Instant and contested: each roll takes an hour, including the primary actor's.
**Dice Pools**:
 *Primary*: Intelligence + Occult vs Manipulation + Subterfuge + Potency.
  *Secondary*: Wits + Investigation (collecting evidence, 1/3, or 0/3 if someone tails the target); Wits + Stealth (tailing target 1/1, or 0/1 if someone collects evidence); Wits + Occult (resource, 0/3).
**Success**: The hunters discern whether the target is an ordinary human, a hunter, or a supernatural creature; if the latter, they learn the type of creature. They also learn one of the following about the target: one Anchor, one Aspiration, the location of their lair or home, or the identity of one character important to her. All participants gain the Informed Condition regarding the target.
**Exceptional Success**: As success, but players learn two specific pieces of information.
**Failure an Dramatic Failure**: The target becomes aware of the investigation and takes on group of secondary actors by surprise with an ambush, an automatically successful supernatural power, or a disadvantageous circumstance.

tactics.name: Called Shot
tactics.desc:
**Action**: Instant and resisted
**Dice Pools**:
  *Primary*: Strength + Weaponry or Dexterity + Firearms - target's Defense.
  *Secondary*: Manipulation + Persuasion or Subterfuge (baiting, 1/2); Strength + Brawl (tacking, 1/2)
**Success**: The opponent suffers the appropriate Tilt for a successful hit on the specified target, and the hunter's attack deals damage as normal with a +1 to his weapon modifier. The target takes a penalty to Initiative equal to the number of participants for the rest of the scene.
**Exceptional Success**: As success, and the Storyteller offers an immediate surrender in exchange for a non-lethal outcome to the scene. If the players accept, the Tactic’s tar- get submits to whatever fate the hunters choose that can be enacted within the current scene, such as capture or giving something up, as long as it doesn’t involve further violence against the target.
**Failure or Dramatic Failure**: The target twists or ducks at the last minute, and the primary actor makes a reflexive attack against the secondary actor closest to the target, ignoring Defense.

rotes.name: Kinetic Blow
rotes.desc:

**Primary Factor**: Potency

Subject's unarmed attacks gain a damage bonus equal to Potency (to a maximum of 5) and deal lethal damage.
**+1 Reach**: spell applies the Knocked Down Tilt.

rotes.name: Cleanse the Body

arcana_attainments.name: Mage Armor - Forces

yantras.name: Dedicated Tool
yantras.desc: A physical implement dedicated to magical workings through ritual and use. **Dice bonus:** +2. The tool must be relevant to the working or Arcana used.

yantras.name: High Speech
yantras.desc: The ancient language of the Supernal, taught to all Awakened. Speaking aloud in High Speech during casting. **Dice bonus:** +2. Cannot be used silently.

yantras.name: Location
yantras.desc: A place with strong sympathy to the spell's target or symbolism. **Dice bonus:** +1 to +3 depending on strength of the connection. Prepared locations take time to establish.

yantras.name: Rune or Diagram
yantras.desc: A symbolic representation of the spell drawn on a surface or in the air. **Dice bonus:** +2. Takes one minute to draw; destroyed after use unless made permanent.

yantras.name: Sacrament
yantras.desc: A physical object with strong connection to the spell's subject — a lock of hair, a prized possession. **Dice bonus:** +2. Consumed or significantly altered in the working.

yantras.name: Symbolic Resonance
yantras.desc: The time, place, or circumstances of the casting align with the spell's intent (casting a curse at midnight, healing at dawn). **Dice bonus:** +1.

yantras.name: Concentration
yantras.desc: The mage spends a full turn in quiet focus before casting, taking no other actions. **Dice bonus:** +2. Broken by damage, distraction, or combat.

magical_tools.name: Order Tool
magical_tools.desc: The iconic implement of the mage's Order — a Mysterium grimoire, a Silver Ladder sceptre, an Arrow blade. **Benefit:** +1 die to all spells while wielded. Cannot be the same as the dedicated tool.

magical_tools.name: Path Tool
magical_tools.desc: A tool aligned to the mage's Path — a Obrimos rod and chalice, an Acanthus wand. **Benefit:** +1 die to Ruling Arcana spells. Distinct from both the dedicated tool and Order tool.

magical_tools.name: Grimoire
magical_tools.desc: A bound text containing recorded spells and magical theory. **Benefit:** Studying a grimoire provides a Yantra bonus for a specific spell it contains. Reading time: one hour minimum.

magical_tools.name: Imbued Item
magical_tools.desc: An object containing a spell held in ready suspension. **Benefit:** Activating the item releases the stored spell without requiring a casting roll. Activation is an instant action.

magical_tools.name: Artifact
magical_tools.desc: A powerful object of Supernal origin, containing a self-sustaining magical effect. **Benefit:** Varies by artifact. Artifacts cannot be created by mages — they are discovered.

disciplines.name: Celerity
disciplines.desc:
**Cost**: None or 1 Vitae per active effect
**Dice Pool**: None
**Action**: None (for persistant effects) or Reflexive (for active effects)
**Duration**: Permanant (for persistant effects) or one turn (for active effects)
**Persistant**: Add the vampire's dots in Celerity to her Defense or to her Dodge roll when defending actively. If a firearms attack denies her normal defense, the attacker still takes a penalty to his attack equal to the vampire's dots in Celerity. A character must still be aware of the incoming attacks and able to move to defend against them.
**Active**: By spending Vitae Celerity can enable one of the following effects (each can only be done once a turn but multiple can be done simultaneously:
- Move to the head of the Initiative queue
- Interrupt the action of another character with a brief action of her own (still limited to 1 instant action).
- Multiply her Speed by dots in Celerity+1

disciplines.name: Majesty: Confidant
disciplines.desc:
**Cost**: None
**Requirement**: The vampire must use Awe on the victim.
**Dice Pool**: Presence + Empathy + Majesty vs Resolve + Blood Potency
**Action**: Contested; resistance is reflective
**Dramatic Failure**: Gain the Swooning Condition for the victim.
**Failure**: No effect.
**Success**: Victim gains the Charmed Condition.
**Exceptional Success**: Victim's Charmed Condition lasts for nights rather than hours.

disciplines.name: Protean: Beast's Skin
disciplines.desc:
**Cost**: 2 Vitae
**Dice Pool**: None
Action: Instant
**Duration**: Infinite
Take the form of an animal the vampire has consumed. Can only take the form of predatory animals, carrion-eaters, plague-carrying beasts, and parasites between Size 1 and 7. A vampire can have a number of forms at the ready equal to her dots in Protean; to add or replace one she must consume the appropriate beast then slumber for a full day and night in her Unmarked Grave. In animal form she takes on the beast't Physical Attributes, Skills, Size, Speed, and Health. She can move, sense, and attack in any way the animal can. She may be unable to use some Physical Merits at the Storyteller's discretion. She can remain in her animal form indefinitely but still needs to consume blood and will be harmed by sunlight. The vampire can use her Disciplines in animal form.

devotions.name: Body of Will
devotions.desc:
**Requirements**: Resiliance 3, Vigor 1
**Cost**: 1 Vitae
Dice Pool: Stamina + Survival + Resiliance
**Action**: Reflexive
For one turn per success, the character suffers no wound penalties. As well, during any turn where he takes damage, he does not need to spend Vitae to activate one effect of Vigor. This Devotion costs 2 Experiences to learn.

vampire_rites.name: Rigor Mortis
vampire_rites.desc:
**Target number of successes**: 5
**Resisted**: Composure
The victim, who must be a vampire within a mile of the ritual, suffers the loss of the reanimating power of Vitae. His next physical action is penalized by -3.

**Cost**: 1 Essence

Add Wisdom Renown to all Emphathy rolls made when interacting with spirits and the Ridden. Can also be used to directly to any spirit you can perceive, revealing symbolic truths. Second and subsequent uses cost 1 Essence each.
**Dramatic Failure**: Unable to read the spirit and the spirit becomes aware of the attempt.

**Failure**: Fail to still body's vital signs
**Succcess**: Still body's vital signs. Appear to be freshly dead, displaying no pulse or respiration, and ceasing natural regeneration. Can still act under this effect with a penalty of 5 - Cunning Renown, appearing as an undead creature.
**Exceptional Success**: Reduce all damage suffered by 1.

rites.name: Chain Rage
rites.desc:
**Wolf Rite**
**Symbols**: Rage, calm, binding, dawn
**Sample Rite**: Certain northerly Scandinavian packs work themselves into a frothing fury udner the light of the new day's sun, scream their anger into etched jars and rend their own flesh until exhausted. Then they hurl themselves into frigid water. (Stamina + Survival).

As long as the Uratha keeps the focus about her person, then achieving five turns of lucidity during a period of Wasu-Im (not continuous) immediately ends the rage. At the end of the month, or should the focus be broken or taken, the Uratha immediately enters Wasu-Im.

help_sections.title: Getting Started
help_sections.content:
Welcome to Mortals+, the Chronicles of Darkness character builder!

Click **Generate Mortal** for a randomised mortal character, or **Generate Blank Mortal** to start from scratch with an empty sheet.

For spirits, ghosts, and other supernatural beings, use **Generate Ephemeral Entity** or **Generate Blank Entity**. Select a Rank first to set the entity's power level.

Once a sheet is open, fill in your character's name and identity fields at the top. All fields save automatically to your browser.

When you're ready to run a scene, use **⚔ Storyteller Mode** in the sidebar to open the live scene workspace.

help_sections.title: Saving, Folders & Tags
help_sections.content:
Click **Save** to store the current character in your browser. Saved characters appear in the **Saves** panel in the sidebar or drawer.

Saves are stored locally in your browser and **will be lost** if you clear your browser data. Use **Export Sheet** to keep a safe copy. You can re-import it on any browser.

**Folders** let you group characters by chronicle, faction, or any category you like. Create a folder using the input at the bottom of the Saves panel. Assign characters to folders using the small dropdown on each save-item row. Folders are collapsible and appear in the Saves panel, tablet drawer, and Storyteller Mode's Add to Scene panel.

**Tags** are freeform labels you can attach to any character. This is useful for cross-cutting labels like `PC`, `NPC`, or `active`. The filter bar at the top of the Saves panel searches by both name and tag. Add tags directly on each character row in the Saves panel.

help_sections.title: File System Storage (Chrome & Edge)
help_sections.content:
In addition to browser storage, you can connect a folder on your device to store characters and library data as real files. This is optional. Browser saves continue to work exactly as before.

**Why use it:**
- Characters stored in a folder survive browser data clears
- No storage limit (browser storage is capped at ~5 MB)
- Sync the folder with another service such as OneDrive to share sheets across devices or with other players

**To connect a folder**, open the **Character Sheet** or **Data Library** panel in the sidebar or drawer. Click the **📁 Connect** button for the type of folder you want to connect, read the one-time advisory about using a dedicated subfolder, then choose your folder.

Once connected, every save writes to both the folder and your browser. The browser copy acts as a live backup. The character list shows characters from both sources in a single unified list.

When you reopen the app, a clickable prompt appears if the folder connection needs reapproval.

**Three folder types:**
- **Characters folder** — each character is saved as a `[name].json` file, the same format as a manual export
- **data.json folder** — place a custom `data.json` here to replace the built-in library for your group. Requires a page reload to take effect
- **Supplement folder** — your Library Editor entries are saved as `supplemental.json` alongside your browser copy

*This feature requires Chrome or Edge. The buttons are visible but inactive on other browsers.*

help_sections.title: Splats & Presets
help_sections.content:
Open **Sheet Configuration** (the button in the sidebar or drawer) to switch between character types, such as Vampire, Werewolf, and Mage. Applying a preset enables all the sections for that splat and hides the ones you don't need.

You can also toggle individual sections on or off within a preset. Any section can be added to any character regardless of splat.

The **Theme** selector at the bottom of the configuration panel changes the sheet's colour scheme to match your splat.

help_sections.title: Layout & Sections
help_sections.content:
Click the **Lock Layout** button to unlock the sheet's layout and enable customisation. Drag any section header to reorder it or move it between the header, left column, right column, and footer. Layout is saved per character.

Click a section header to collapse or expand it. **Collapse all** and **Expand all** buttons are in the toolbar.

Dot tracks are clicked to set a rating. Health boxes cycle through Bashing (B), Lethal (L), and Aggravated (A) damage on each click. Right-click or click a filled box to clear it.

help_sections.title: Data Library
help_sections.content:
The **Library Editor** (Data Library → ✎ Edit library) lets you add custom entries to any section's ability list — homebrew merits, weapons from the rulebook, custom conditions, and so on.

Select a section type from the dropdown, then click **+ New entry** to add your own. You can also **Override** any base library entry to replace it with a modified version.

Entries on your character sheet that aren't in the library yet show a small **sync** button in their header row. Click it to add that entry to your supplement immediately — no need to open the editor separately.

Use **Export** in the editor to save your supplement as a backup file. Import it on any browser to restore or share your entries. Your supplement is stored in your browser. Export regularly to avoid losing it if you clear your browser data.
